services.title: Home Interior Design
services.summary: Apartments and family homes planned around storage, light and daily routines.
services.description: We design complete apartments and family homes, from space planning to the last cushion. Every plan starts with how your household actually moves through the day, then we shape storage, lighting and finishes around it.

services.title: Villa Interior Design
services.summary: Large-format interiors that connect indoor rooms with gardens and terraces.
services.description: Villas give us room to work with volume, daylight and outdoor views. We design a consistent language across every floor, so the entrance, living areas and bedrooms feel like one home.

services.title: Duplex Interior Design
services.summary: Two-level homes with a staircase, voids and zoning that feel connected.
services.description: A duplex needs a plan for two floors that still feels like one home. We separate quiet and social zones, treat the staircase as a design feature and keep sightlines open between levels.

services.title: Bungalow Interior Design
services.summary: Single-storey living with generous, flowing rooms and strong garden links.
services.description: Bungalows reward a calm, open plan. We focus on circulation, natural ventilation and materials that age well, so the home stays comfortable through every season.

services.title: Office Interior Design
services.summary: Workplaces that support focus, meetings and the way your team really works.
services.description: We design offices around teams, not desks. That means quiet focus areas, flexible meeting rooms, acoustic comfort and a reception that tells clients who you are.

services.title: Penthouse Interior Design
services.summary: Top-floor residences and show suites built for views, entertaining and privacy.
services.description: Penthouses are about the view and the way guests move through the space. We frame the skyline, plan entertaining areas and keep private rooms quiet and well separated.

items.title: Luxury Modern Living Room
items.summary: A blend of contemporary elegance and comfort, this living room design combines clean lines with warm furniture.
items.description: The brief asked for a calm living space that could host twenty guests and still feel intimate on a quiet evening. We opened the plan, added a fluted wall behind the media unit and layered warm lighting at three heights.

items.title: High-End Space for a Tech Startup
items.summary: A sleek, modern office designed to foster creativity and productivity, with a focus on team comfort.
items.description: For a 40-person team we planned open desks, three focus rooms and a long shared table that doubles as the all-hands space. Acoustic panels and soft lighting keep the room quiet.

items.title: Exclusive Boutique Store Design
items.summary: For this high-end retail store, we created an immersive shopping experience using luxurious finishes.
items.description: Display joinery in pale oak, brushed brass rails and indirect lighting let the products lead. Fitting rooms are sized generously and lit for true colour.

items.title: Sage Garden Villa
items.summary: A three-storey villa with soft green accents and a double-height living hall.
items.description: Stone floors, linen curtains and quiet greens connect the interior to the garden. The double-height hall is lit by a sculptural pendant that anchors the staircase.

items.title: Skyline Penthouse
items.summary: A top-floor residence arranged around the skyline with an entertaining kitchen and bar.
items.description: Furniture sits low to protect the view. A long island joins the kitchen and dining area, and a dark joinery bar anchors the terrace doors.

items.title: Sand Duplex Home
items.summary: Two floors linked by a slim timber staircase and a shared light well.
items.description: Sandy plaster walls, pale oak joinery and a light well that pulls daylight to the lower floor give the duplex a single, calm identity.

items.title: Oak and Brass Cafe
items.summary: A neighbourhood cafe with a long oak counter, brass details and soft pendant lighting.
items.description: Seating is mixed so the room works for solo laptops and group catch-ups. The counter is the centrepiece and the lighting stays warm all day.

items.title: Clay Restaurant
items.summary: A 70-seat restaurant with textured plaster walls and an open kitchen pass.
items.description: Textured clay-tone plaster, cushioned banquettes and low pendants create a warm room that stays comfortable at full capacity.

items.title: Quiet Bungalow
items.summary: A single-storey home with a deep veranda and rooms that open to the garden.
items.description: Cross-ventilation, deep eaves and natural stone keep the bungalow cool. Every principal room has a direct view of the garden.

items.title: Studio Beauty Parlour
items.summary: A bright salon with mirror-lit stations, private treatment rooms and a calm waiting lounge.
items.description: Mirror-lit stations, easy-clean surfaces and a soft sage palette keep the salon practical and relaxing.

items.title: Midnight Study
items.summary: A deep-toned study with floor-to-ceiling shelving and a built-in desk.
items.description: A dark, enveloping palette with warm task lighting makes the study a room you want to stay in. Shelving reaches the ceiling and hides the cabling.

items.title: Corporate Reception Suite
items.summary: A reception and boardroom suite that sets the tone for an investment firm.
items.description: Stone, walnut and quiet lighting give the suite weight without feeling cold. The boardroom seats sixteen and doubles as a presentation space.

tabs.heading: Designing homes since 2017
tabs.body:
Lavish Interiors began as a two-person studio in Dhaka and has grown into a team of designers, engineers and site supervisors working across Dhaka and Chittagong.

We stay small enough to know every project by name, and organised enough to deliver on schedule.

tabs.heading: Design that starts with your routine
tabs.body:
We begin by learning how you live or work, then plan the space around that. Materials are chosen to age well and be easy to maintain.

Every project follows the same four steps, so you always know what comes next.

We inspect the finished space with you and fix every snag before handover.

blog.title: Eight storage ideas that make a small apartment feel larger
blog.excerpt: Built-in storage, clear sightlines and lighter finishes do more for a small home than another piece of furniture.
body: Small apartments rarely lack style. They lack places to put things. The fastest way to make a compact home feel bigger is to move everyday items out of sight.
Start with full-height wardrobes and a bench with storage in the entry. Use the space under beds and window seats, and keep the floor clear so the eye reads more area.
Finally, choose a limited palette. Light walls, matching joinery and consistent flooring make the rooms read as one continuous space.

blog.title: How to choose lighting for a living room
blog.excerpt: Layer ambient, task and accent light, and put each layer on its own switch.
body: A single ceiling light flattens a room. Good living rooms use three layers: ambient light for general use, task light for reading, and accent light for walls and artwork.
Warm white at about 2700K to 3000K suits evening living spaces. Put every layer on its own switch or dimmer so the room can change from daytime to movie night.
Plan the lighting before the furniture. Wiring is easy to change on paper and expensive to change after the walls are finished.

blog.title: Office design that helps people focus
blog.excerpt: Acoustics, zoning and daylight matter more than the desk layout.
body: Open offices fail when everything happens in one noisy room. Separate focus areas from collaboration areas and give each its own acoustic treatment.
Place quiet desks away from kitchens and meeting rooms, and keep at least one small room free for calls.
Finally, give people daylight. Placing desks near windows and meeting rooms in the core improves comfort for the whole team.

blog.title: Materials that last in Bangladesh's humid climate
blog.excerpt: Moisture-resistant boards, sealed stone and good ventilation protect interiors for years.
body: Humidity is the biggest test for interior materials in Bangladesh. Choose moisture-resistant boards for kitchens and bathrooms, and seal natural stone properly.
Veneered or laminated surfaces on marine-grade plywood hold up far better than standard boards.
Ventilation matters as much as material. Plan air flow in wardrobes and bathrooms so moisture can leave.

blog.title: How to brief an interior designer
blog.excerpt: A clear brief saves weeks. Here is what to prepare before the first meeting.
body: Bring your floor plan, a rough budget range and photos of rooms you like. Tell us who lives in the space and what annoys you about it today.
List the must-haves and the nice-to-haves separately. This helps us protect the things that matter most when costs change.
Finally, share your timeline. Moving dates and events decide how we schedule procurement and site work.

blog.title: Building a timeless luxury palette
blog.excerpt: Neutral bases, one natural material and a few deep accents age better than trends.
body: Timeless interiors start with a quiet base: warm whites, stone and soft greys. They let materials and light do the talking.
Add one natural material such as oak or marble, and repeat it in a few places so the room feels deliberate.
Keep bold colours in cushions, art and accessories. They are the easiest things to change later.
